question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation to isolate the logarithmic term:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{log}_{3}⁡(x+24)}{3} & =2 \\ {log}_{3}⁡(x+24) & =6\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The base of the logarithm is $3,$ so we use this base for the exponentiation as well:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{3}⁡(x+24) & =6 \\ {3}^{{log}_{3}⁡(x+24)} & ={3}^{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get ${3}^{{log}_{3}⁡(x+24)}=x+24.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}x+24 & ={3}^{6} \\ x+24 & =729 \\ x & =705.\end{aligned}
$$
